content.title: About
content.content: Pannetone is a traditional Italian sweet bread made from a yeasted dough enriched with raisins, candied citrus peel and often nuts. It has a light, airy crumb, a fragrant sweet flavor, and a distinctive tall, dome‑shaped appearance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pannetone originates from Milan, where it is traditionally baked for Christmas and New Year celebrations.
Classic recipes include candied orange and lemon peel and raisins, but modern versions may contain chocolate, nuts or dried fruits.
A popular legend says a baker created pannetone as a love gift to impress his beloved.
The original recipe uses “soft” butter, which gives the cake its tender texture.
In Italy pannetone is often served with hot chocolate or sweet wine.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat, making it a quick source of energy.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough contains thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Raisins and candied peel add fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Citrus candied peel is high in vitamin C and flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Compared with many sweets, pannetone typically contains little salt.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The large amount of sugar makes pannetone calorie‑dense and can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional recipes use wheat flour, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Dried fruit sensitivity
items.content: Raisins and candied peel may cause stomach discomfort in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of butter and sugar, pannetone is fairly caloric; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice pannetone and serve it as a dessert or snack. It can be toasted and buttered, added to yogurt, ice cream, or used in tiramisu and bread pudding recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pannetone in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze it, wrapped tightly in plastic film.
